Type 2 Diabetes.description: Type 2 Diabetes is a progressive endocrine-metabolic disorder characterized by peripheral insulin resistance, compensatory hyperinsulinemia, and progressive pancreatic beta-cell exhaustion. Over time, persistent hyperglycemia leads to widespread microvascular (nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy) and macrovascular (cardiovascular disease, stroke) damage.
Type 2 Diabetes.recommended_action: Consult an endocrinologist. Implement medical nutrition therapy, structured physical activity (≥150 min/wk), and monitor HbA1c every 3 months.
causes: Pancreatic beta-cell secretory defect
Skeletal muscle and hepatic insulin receptor desensitization
Adipocyte hypertrophy and chronic low-grade systemic inflammation
Sedentary lifestyle and visceral adiposity (BMI ≥ 25-30 kg/m²)
Genetic polymorphism (TCF7L2, KCNJ11, PPARG variants)
diagnostic_methods: Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) ≥ 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) on two separate occasions
Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) ≥ 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) standardized assay
2-Hour Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT) ≥ 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L)
Random plasma glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL with classic hyperglycemia symptoms
treatment_options: First-line Biguanide (Metformin) to suppress hepatic gluconeogenesis
GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide, Liraglutide) for glucose-dependent insulin secretion & weight loss
SGLT-2 Inhibitors (Empagliflozin, Dapagliflozin) for renal glucose excretion & cardioprotection
DPP-4 Inhibitors & Basal/Prandial Insulin therapy when beta-cell reserves decline
Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) and individualized medical nutrition therapy
prevention_strategies: 7% sustained body weight reduction through caloric deficit
Minimum 150 minutes/week of moderate-to-vigorous aerobic exercise + resistance training
High-fiber Mediterranean or low-glycemic dietary pattern (>30g fiber daily)
Annual fasting metabolic panel and HbA1c screening for all adults ≥ 35 years
possible_complications: Diabetic Retinopathy (leading cause of adult-onset blindness)
Diabetic Nephropathy (end-stage renal disease requiring hemodialysis)
Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy & neuropathic foot ulceration
Accelerated Atherosclerosis (2-4x higher risk of myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke)
Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD) and lower extremity amputation

biomarkers.name: Fasting Plasma Glucose
biomarkers.interpretation: Elevated hepatic gluconeogenesis reflecting overnight basal insulin resistance.

biomarkers.name: Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c)
biomarkers.interpretation: Weighted 90-day average glycemic exposure with glycosylation of erythrocyte hemoglobin.

biomarkers.name: HOMA-IR (Insulin Resistance Index)
biomarkers.interpretation: Significant cellular receptor resistance demanding supra-physiological insulin secretion.

biomarkers.name: Body Mass Index (BMI)
biomarkers.interpretation: Class I obesity promoting lipotoxicity, free fatty acid elevation, and chronic inflammation.

stages.title: Subclinical Insulin Resistance
stages.criteria: Normal fasting glucose (<100 mg/dL), normal HbA1c (<5.7%), but elevated fasting insulin (>12 µIU/mL).
stages.symptoms: Postprandial somnolence, mild central adiposity, carbohydrate cravings.
stages.reversibility: 100% Reversible with nutritional modification, intermittent fasting, and zone-2 aerobic conditioning.

stages.title: Impaired Fasting Glucose / Prediabetes
stages.criteria: FPG 100–125 mg/dL or HbA1c 5.7%–6.4%. First phase insulin response decreased by ~50%.
stages.symptoms: Mild fatigue, skin tags, occasional blurred vision after high-glycemic meals.
stages.reversibility: High reversibility (~80%) through intensive lifestyle intervention (Diabetes Prevention Program protocol).

stages.title: Overt Type 2 Diabetes
stages.criteria: FPG ≥ 126 mg/dL or HbA1c ≥ 6.5%. Pancreatic beta-cell function reduced by ~70%.
stages.symptoms: Polyuria, polydipsia, lethargy, slow wound healing, recurrent fungal infections.
stages.reversibility: Achievable clinical remission in early disease (<5 yrs) via substantial weight loss (>10-15kg) or bariatric metabolic surgery.

stages.title: Complicated Diabetes with End-Organ Damage
stages.criteria: HbA1c > 8.5% with established micro/macrovascular target organ injury (eGFR decline, retinopathy).
stages.symptoms: Peripheral neuropathic numbness, vision degradation, proteinuria, exertional angina.
stages.reversibility: Organ damage is largely irreversible; management focuses on secondary prevention and stabilization.

early_warning.sign: Postprandial reactive drowsiness
early_warning.mechanism: Hypoglycemic rebound following exaggerated insulin surge

early_warning.sign: Nocturnal polyuria (waking 2+ times to urinate)
early_warning.mechanism: Osmotic diuresis as blood glucose exceeds renal threshold (180 mg/dL)

early_warning.sign: Acanthosis Nigricans (dark velvety skin on neck/axillae)
early_warning.mechanism: Excess insulin binding to IGF-1 receptors stimulating keratinocyte proliferation

early_warning.sign: Persistent thirst despite continuous fluid intake
early_warning.mechanism: Hypothalamic osmoreceptor stimulation driven by hyperosmolar serum

acute_emergency.sign: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) / Fruity breath & vomiting
acute_emergency.mechanism: Severe insulin deficiency causing uncontrolled lipolysis and toxic ketone accumulation

acute_emergency.sign: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS, glucose >600 mg/dL)
acute_emergency.mechanism: Profound dehydration, hyperosmolality, and neurological alteration/stupor

acute_emergency.sign: Severe Hypoglycemia (<54 mg/dL with confusion/seizure)
acute_emergency.mechanism: Neuroglycopenia from medication/insulin mismatch

acute_emergency.sign: Non-healing blackened lower extremity ulcer with fever
acute_emergency.mechanism: Diabetic microvascular gangrene and necrotizing soft-tissue infection

target_organs.damage_mechanism: Microaneurysms, macular edema, and neovascularization from pericyte loss
Glomerular basement membrane thickening, nodular glomerulosclerosis (Kimmelstiel-Wilson)
Sorbitol accumulation via polyol pathway and endoneurial microvascular ischemia
Accelerated atherogenesis via advanced glycation end-products (AGEs) and endothelial dysfunction

dos.action: Adhere strictly to low-glycemic Mediterranean or low-carb meal plans
dos.detail: Prioritize cruciferous vegetables, legumes, wild salmon, and healthy monounsaturated fats.

dos.action: Engage in postprandial 15-minute brisk walking after major meals
dos.detail: Directly activates GLUT4 glucose transporters in skeletal muscle independent of insulin.

dos.action: Take prescribed Metformin / GLP-1 / SGLT-2 therapies consistently
dos.detail: Never discontinue antihyperglycemic therapies without physician supervision.

dos.action: Inspect soles and interdigital spaces daily with a mirror
dos.detail: Detect minor blisters or erythema early to prevent neuropathic ulcer progression.

donts.action: Avoid sodas, sweetened teas, commercial juices, and energy drinks
donts.detail: Free fructose and sucrose bypass hepatic regulation, inducing rapid hyperglycemia and steatosis.

donts.action: Avoid uninterrupted sitting exceeding 45 minutes
donts.detail: Prolonged inactivity downregulates lipoprotein lipase and impairs peripheral insulin sensitivity.

donts.action: Never walk barefoot indoors or outdoors
donts.detail: Subtle neuropathic loss of sensation can permit traumatic puncture wounds without pain perception.

donts.action: Avoid tobacco smoking and vaping completely
donts.detail: Nicotine directly constricts microvessels and exacerbates peripheral vascular disease twofold.

diagnostic_tests.importance: Gold standard 90-day glycemic control index.
Screens for incipient diabetic nephropathy and drug clearance safety.
Most sensitive earliest marker of glomerular hyperfiltration and damage.

diagnostic_tests.target: No retinal microaneurysms or macular exudates
diagnostic_tests.importance: Detects asymptomatic early retinopathy prior to irreversible visual loss.

Hypertension.description: Hypertension is a chronic hemodynamic disorder characterized by persistent elevation of systemic arterial pressure (systolic ≥ 130 mmHg and/or diastolic ≥ 80 mmHg). Known as the 'silent killer' due to its insidious, asymptomatic progression, it induces sustained arterial shear stress, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, and end-organ microvascular remodeling.
Hypertension.recommended_action: Schedule physician consultation. Institute sodium restriction (<2,000 mg/day), regular aerobic exercise, and initiate pharmacotherapy if BP remains ≥ 130/80 mmHg with elevated cardiovascular risk.
causes: Excessive dietary sodium and reduced dietary potassium intake
Sympathetic nervous system hyperactivation and blunted baroreceptor sensitivity
Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) dysregulation
Arterial stiffening and endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability decline
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) with recurrent nocturnal hypoxia surges
diagnostic_methods: Serial in-clinic blood pressure measurements (≥2 separate occasions using calibrated cuff)
24-Hour Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring (ABPM) — clinical gold standard
Home Blood Pressure Monitoring (HBPM) twice daily for 7 consecutive days
12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) to assess Left Ventricular Hypertrophy (Sokolow-Lyon index)
treatment_options: ACE Inhibitors (Lisinopril) or Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers (Losartan, Valsartan)
Dihydropyridine Calcium Channel Blockers (Amlodipine) for peripheral vasodilation
Thiazide/Thiazide-like Diuretics (Chlorthalidone, Indapamide) for natriuresis
Beta-Blockers (Carvedilol, Metoprolol succinate) if co-existing coronary artery disease or heart failure
DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) dietary pattern
prevention_strategies: Reduce dietary sodium to < 1,500 - 2,000 mg/day and increase potassium to 3,500 - 5,000 mg/day
Maintain body weight in optimal BMI range (18.5 - 24.9 kg/m²)
Engage in 150 minutes/week of moderate aerobic training plus isometric handgrip exercises
Limit alcohol intake to ≤ 1 standard drink daily for women, ≤ 2 for men
possible_complications: Ischemic and Hemorrhagic Cerebrovascular Stroke
Myocardial Infarction and Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis leading to Chronic Kidney Disease
Thoracic and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm & Dissection
Hypertensive Retinopathy and visual impairment

biomarkers.name: Systolic Blood Pressure (SBP)
biomarkers.interpretation: Elevated peak systolic pressure reflecting arterial wall stiffness and high stroke volume resistance.

biomarkers.name: Diastolic Blood Pressure (DBP)
biomarkers.interpretation: Elevated baseline peripheral vascular resistance during ventricular diastole.

biomarkers.name: Pulse Pressure (SBP - DBP)
biomarkers.interpretation: Arterial compliance marker; widened pulse pressure correlates with large-artery atherosclerosis.

biomarkers.name: Resting Heart Rate
biomarkers.interpretation: Elevated sympathetic adrenergic drive contributing to sustained vascular tension.

stages.title: Elevated Blood Pressure
stages.criteria: Systolic 120–129 mmHg AND Diastolic < 80 mmHg.
stages.symptoms: Typically asymptomatic; slight decrease in nocturnal dipping on 24h ABPM.
stages.reversibility: 100% Reversible with sodium reduction, potassium supplementation, and physical exercise.

stages.title: Stage 1 Essential Hypertension
stages.criteria: Systolic 130–139 mmHg OR Diastolic 80–89 mmHg.
stages.symptoms: Occasional mild tension headache, mild post-exertional fatigue.
stages.reversibility: High reversibility through lifestyle change + low-dose single antihypertensive agent.

stages.title: Stage 2 Severe Hypertension
stages.criteria: Systolic ≥ 140 mmHg OR Diastolic ≥ 90 mmHg.
stages.symptoms: Frequent morning headaches, dizziness, palpitations, visual blurriness.
stages.reversibility: Requires dual-agent pharmacotherapy; vascular remodeling can be stabilized and halted.

stages.title: Hypertensive Crisis & End-Organ Damage
stages.criteria: Systolic > 180 mmHg and/or Diastolic > 120 mmHg with acute target organ compromise.
stages.symptoms: Severe chest pain, dyspnea, neurological deficit, confusion, hematuria.
stages.reversibility: Medical emergency requiring immediate parenteral ICU blood pressure titration.

early_warning.sign: Occipital morning tension headache
early_warning.mechanism: Elevated intracranial capillary pressure during recumbent sleep

early_warning.sign: Pulsatile tinnitus (rhythmic ear whooshing)
early_warning.mechanism: Turbulent blood flow through narrowed carotid artery and petrous bone canal

early_warning.sign: Subtle exercise intolerance and shortness of breath
early_warning.mechanism: Impaired left ventricular diastolic relaxation due to increased afterload

early_warning.sign: Spontaneous anterior epistaxis (nosebleed)
early_warning.mechanism: Rupture of Kiesselbach's plexus submucosal arterioles under high hydrostatic pressure

acute_emergency.sign: Thunderclap explosive headache with confusion
acute_emergency.mechanism: Hypertensive encephalopathy and breakdown of blood-brain barrier autoregulation

acute_emergency.sign: Severe tearing chest pain radiating to mid-back
acute_emergency.mechanism: Acute aortic dissection driven by peak systolic wall tension

acute_emergency.sign: Sudden unilateral facial droop or arm weakness
acute_emergency.mechanism: Acute hemorrhagic or ischemic cerebrovascular accident (Stroke)

acute_emergency.sign: Acute dyspnea with pink frothy sputum
acute_emergency.mechanism: Flash pulmonary edema from sudden left ventricular decompensation

target_organs.damage_mechanism: Charcot-Bouchard microaneurysms, lacunar infarcts, and intracerebral hemorrhage
Concentric hypertrophy, myofibrillar disarray, leading to diastolic heart failure (HFpEF)
Hyaline arteriolosclerosis, ischemic nephron atrophy, and glomerulosclerosis
Elastin fragmentation, media thinning, and aneurysm formation

dos.action: Limit total daily sodium intake strictly below 1,500 - 2,000 mg
dos.detail: Cook fresh whole foods and eliminate processed deli meats, canned soups, and salty condiments.

dos.action: Consume potassium-dense foods (spinach, avocados, white beans)
dos.detail: Potassium promotes renal sodium excretion and induces systemic vascular smooth muscle relaxation.

dos.action: Measure resting BP twice daily: 1 min after waking, and before bed
dos.detail: Rest seated for 5 minutes with arm supported at heart level before recording values.

dos.action: Practice slow paced diaphragmatic breathing (6 breaths/min) for 10 min
dos.detail: Upregulates vagal tone and acutely suppresses sympathetic vasopressor outflow.

donts.action: Never abruptly stop taking antihypertensive medications
donts.detail: Abrupt withdrawal (especially beta-blockers or clonidine) triggers severe rebound hypertensive crisis.

donts.action: Avoid chronic NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Celecoxib)
donts.detail: NSAIDs inhibit renal prostaglandins, causing sodium retention and raising BP by 5-10 mmHg.

donts.action: Avoid cold medications containing Pseudoephedrine or Phenylephrine
donts.detail: Potent alpha-1 agonists that directly constrict systemic blood vessels and spike arterial pressure.

donts.action: Avoid binge drinking and excessive alcohol consumption
donts.detail: More than 2 drinks/day triggers sympathetic activation and cortisol-mediated vasoconstriction.

diagnostic_tests.importance: Gold standard to diagnose true hypertension and rule out white-coat or masked hypertension.

diagnostic_tests.target: Normal voltage; no Left Ventricular Hypertrophy or strain pattern
diagnostic_tests.importance: Assesses presence of hypertensive heart disease and arrhythmia risk.
Evaluates kidney function and checks safety for ACEi/ARB and diuretic therapy.
Monitors potassium homeostasis critical for patients on RAAS inhibitors and diuretics.

types: CKD Stage 1 (Kidney damage with normal GFR)
Chronic Kidney Disease.description: Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD) is defined as persistent structural or functional abnormalities of the kidneys for > 3 months, manifested by an Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) < 60 mL/min/1.73m² or persistent markers of kidney damage (most commonly urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio ≥ 30 mg/g). As functional nephrons undergo apoptotic loss and interstitial fibrosis, the kidneys progressively lose their ability to filter metabolic toxins, regulate fluid-electrolyte balance, and produce erythropoietin.
Chronic Kidney Disease.recommended_action: Immediate nephrology consultation. Optimize blood pressure (<120 mmHg SBP with SGLT2i + ACEi/ARB), reduce dietary sodium and phosphorus, and monitor renal function panel quarterly.
causes: Diabetic Glomerulosclerosis (responsible for ~40% of all CKD cases)
Hypertensive Nephrosclerosis with arteriolar hyalinosis (~25% of cases)
Glomerulonephritis (IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, FSGS)
Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) and inherited cystic nephropathies
Chronic use of nephrotoxic medications (NSAIDs, aminoglycosides, proton-pump inhibitors)
symptoms: Fatigue and weakness from renal anemia
diagnostic_methods: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) calculated via CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine equation
Spot Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (uACR) on early morning specimen
Serum Creatinine, Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN), and Serum Cystatin C
Renal Ultrasonography to assess kidney size, cortical thinning, and hydronephrosis
Percutaneous Renal Biopsy when etiology of glomerulonephritis is uncertain
treatment_options: SGLT-2 Inhibitors (Dapagliflozin, Empagliflozin) for profound nephroprotection & eGFR slope preservation
ACE Inhibitors or ARBs titrated to maximally tolerated doses to reduce intraglomerular hypertension
Non-steroidal Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonists (Finerenone) to suppress renal fibrosis
Recombinant Erythropoietin (EPO) and IV iron supplementation for renal normochromic anemia
Phosphate binders and active Vitamin D (Calcitriol) for mineral bone disease management
Renal Replacement Therapy: Hemodialysis, Peritoneal Dialysis, or Pre-emptive Kidney Transplantation
prevention_strategies: Strict glycemic control (HbA1c < 6.5-7.0%) to prevent diabetic microvascular injury
Target systolic blood pressure < 120 mmHg utilizing renal-protective antihypertensive regimens
Avoid all nephrotoxic over-the-counter NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Ketorolac)
Moderate dietary protein intake to 0.6 - 0.8 g/kg/day in non-dialysis CKD patients
possible_complications: End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) requiring lifelong dialysis or renal transplantation
Accelerated Cardiovascular Disease (vascular calcification and sudden cardiac death)
Secondary Hyperparathyroidism and CKD-Mineral Bone Disorder (osteodystrophy, fractures)
Refractory Hyperkalemia (> 6.0 mEq/L) causing lethal cardiac arrhythmias
Metabolic Acidosis and severe protein-energy wasting

biomarkers.name: Estimated GFR (eGFR)
biomarkers.interpretation: Substantial nephron loss corresponding to Stage 3a/3b Chronic Kidney Disease.

biomarkers.name: Serum Creatinine
biomarkers.interpretation: Accumulation of muscular metabolic waste reflecting markedly compromised glomerular filtration.

biomarkers.name: Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratio (uACR)
biomarkers.interpretation: Severe macroalbuminuria indicating podocyte breakdown and glomerular barrier failure.

biomarkers.name: Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN)
biomarkers.interpretation: Impaired clearance of nitrogenous protein catabolites contributing to uremic symptoms.

stages.title: Kidney Damage with Normal or High GFR
stages.criteria: eGFR ≥ 90 mL/min/1.73m² with persistent proteinuria (uACR ≥ 30 mg/g) or structural defect.
stages.symptoms: Asymptomatic; preserved urine output, normal serum creatinine.
stages.reversibility: Disease stabilization possible with glycemic and blood pressure optimization.

stages.title: Kidney Damage with Mild GFR Reduction
stages.criteria: eGFR 60–89 mL/min/1.73m² with persistent kidney damage markers > 3 months.
stages.symptoms: Subtle nocturia, mild fatigue, borderline elevated blood pressure.
stages.reversibility: Nephroprotective regimens (SGLT2i + ACEi) can slow annual eGFR decline to near-normal aging rates.

stages.title: Moderate GFR Reduction (Stages 3a & 3b)
stages.criteria: eGFR 30–59 mL/min/1.73m² (3a: 45-59, 3b: 30-44). Significant nephron fibrosis.
stages.symptoms: Peripheral pedal edema, mild normochromic anemia, bone pain, elevated parathyroid hormone.
stages.reversibility: Irreversible structural loss; intervention centers on slowing progression and preventing CVD death.

stages.title: Severe GFR Reduction & Kidney Failure (Stages 4 & 5)
stages.criteria: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m² (Stage 5 / ESRD: eGFR < 15 mL/min/1.73m²).
stages.symptoms: Severe uremia, refractory nausea, pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, profound anemia.
stages.reversibility: End-stage organ failure requiring dialysis initiation or vascular access creation for renal transplant.

early_warning.sign: Persistent foamy, frothy urine
early_warning.mechanism: Glomerular filtration of albumin lowering surface tension in toilet bowl water

early_warning.sign: Bilateral pedal and ankle edema (sock indentation marks)
early_warning.mechanism: Sodium and water retention alongside decreased oncotic pressure from proteinuria

early_warning.sign: Nocturnal polyuria (waking repeatedly to void dilute urine)
early_warning.mechanism: Loss of medullary osmotic gradient and impaired renal concentrating capacity

early_warning.sign: Unexplained chronic fatigue and pallor
early_warning.mechanism: Peritubular interstitial fibroblast destruction blunting erythropoietin secretion

acute_emergency.sign: Severe dyspnea and orthopnea (cannot lie flat)
acute_emergency.mechanism: Acute pulmonary alveolar edema from severe hypervolemia and fluid overload

acute_emergency.sign: Palpitations and muscle flaccidity / weakness
acute_emergency.mechanism: Severe hyperkalemia (K+ > 6.5 mEq/L) threatening peaked T-waves and ventricular arrest

acute_emergency.sign: Asterixis ('flapping tremor' of outstretched hands) & confusion
acute_emergency.mechanism: Uremic encephalopathy from systemic accumulation of neurotoxic nitrogenous wastes

acute_emergency.sign: Pleuritic chest pain with pericardial friction rub
acute_emergency.mechanism: Uremic pericarditis requiring urgent emergency hemodialysis

target_organs.damage_mechanism: Glomerulosclerosis, tubulointerstitial fibrosis, and tubular atrophy
Medial vascular calcification, left ventricular hypertrophy, and accelerated atheroma
Renal osteodystrophy via hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, and high PTH
Erythropoietin deficiency and uremic suppression of erythroid colony formation

dos.action: Maintain systolic BP < 120 mmHg using renal-protective medications
dos.detail: Prioritize SGLT2 inhibitors and ACEi/ARBs to reduce intraglomerular capillary hypertension.

dos.action: Moderate protein intake to 0.6 - 0.8 grams per kg ideal body weight daily
dos.detail: Reduces nitrogenous waste generation and lowers intraglomerular hyperfiltration stress.

dos.action: Limit sodium strictly below 1,500 mg/day to manage hypervolemia
dos.detail: Reduces reliance on high-dose loop diuretics and prevents peripheral edema surges.

dos.action: Check serum creatinine, potassium, and eGFR every 3 months
dos.detail: Enables rapid detection of acute-on-chronic kidney injury or hyperkalemic spikes.

donts.action: Never take Ibuprofen, Naproxen, Diclofenac, or Ketorolac
donts.detail: NSAIDs selectively constrict afferent renal arterioles, precipitously crashing eGFR.

donts.action: Avoid dark colas, processed cheeses, and phosphate-additive foods
donts.detail: Failing kidneys cannot excrete phosphorus, triggering vascular calcification and bone disease.

donts.action: Avoid IV iodinated contrast scans unless medically emergent
donts.detail: Contrast-induced acute tubular necrosis causes severe irreversible nephron death in CKD.

donts.action: Avoid unregulated herbal cleanses and remedies (e.g. Aristolochia)
donts.detail: Numerous unregulated botanical extracts contain potent nephrotoxins that accelerate interstitial fibrosis.

diagnostic_tests.importance: Primary clinical metric for disease staging and monitoring progression.
Surrogate endpoint for kidney disease survival and treatment efficacy.
Prevents life-threatening hyperkalemic cardiac arrhythmias.
Monitors mineral bone disorder and guides phosphate binder/calcitriol therapy.

COPD.description: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is a progressive, life-threatening inflammatory lung condition characterized by persistent airflow limitation that is not fully reversible (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70). Chronic exposure to toxic particles (principally cigarette smoke) causes small airway remodeling (bronchiolitis) and destruction of the alveolar parenchyma (emphysema), severely impairing alveolar gas exchange and leading to air trapping, hyperinflation, and chronic hypoxemia.
COPD.recommended_action: Consult a pulmonologist. Immediate and absolute smoking cessation, initiate dual long-acting bronchodilator therapy (LAMA/LABA), enroll in pulmonary rehabilitation, and obtain annual vaccinations.
causes: Cigarette, cigar, or pipe smoking (causative in 80–90% of industrialized cases)
Occupational exposure to organic dusts, mineral dusts, and chemical vapors
Biomass fuel combustion for cooking/heating in poorly ventilated environments
Severe genetic Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency (AATD) causing unchecked neutrophil elastase
Impaired childhood lung development and history of severe pediatric respiratory infections
symptoms: Chronic, progressive dyspnea (worsening with physical exertion)
Anorexia and unintended weight loss in advanced disease
diagnostic_methods: Post-Bronchodilator Spirometry: FEV1/FVC < 0.70 confirms persistent airflow obstruction (GOLD criterion)
High-Resolution Computed Tomography (HRCT) of the chest to quantify centrilobular and panacinar emphysema
Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLCO) to measure alveolar-capillary membrane gas exchange
Arterial Blood Gas (ABG) analysis to detect hypoxemia (PaO2 < 60 mmHg) and hypercapnia (PaCO2 > 45 mmHg)
Serum Alpha-1 Antitrypsin level screening in all newly diagnosed COPD patients
treatment_options: Dual Long-Acting Bronchodilators: LAMA (Tiotropium, Umeclidinium) + LABA (Formoterol, Vilanterol)
Inhaled Corticosteroids (ICS: Fluticasone, Budesonide) for patients with high blood eosinophils (≥300 cells/µL) or recurrent exacerbations
Phosphodiesterase-4 (PDE4) Inhibitors (Roflumilast) for chronic bronchitis with frequent flare-ups
Long-Term Oxygen Therapy (LTOT ≥ 15 hrs/day) for resting severe hypoxemia (SpO2 ≤ 88% or PaO2 ≤ 55 mmHg)
Comprehensive Pulmonary Rehabilitation including exercise conditioning and pursed-lip breathing training
Non-Invasive Positive Pressure Ventilation (NIV / BiPAP) for chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure
prevention_strategies: Complete and permanent smoking cessation (pharmacotherapy: Varenicline, Bupropion, Nicotine replacement)
Eliminate second-hand smoke exposure and improve indoor air filtration
Wear certified N95 / HEPA particulate respirators in occupational dust environments
Annual Influenza vaccination, Pneumococcal conjugate (PCV20), COVID-19, and RSV immunization
possible_complications: Acute Exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD) requiring emergency hospitalization and ventilatory support
Chronic Respiratory Failure (hypoxemic and hypercapnic)
Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension and Cor Pulmonale (right-sided congestive heart failure)
Secondary Spontaneous Pneumothorax from rupture of apical emphysematous bullae
High incidence of Bronchogenic Lung Carcinoma and skeletal muscle sarcopenia

biomarkers.name: FEV1 / FVC Ratio (Post-Bronchodilator)
biomarkers.interpretation: Hallmark diagnostic spirometric threshold establishing irreversible expiratory airflow obstruction.

biomarkers.name: FEV1 % Predicted (GOLD Severity)
biomarkers.interpretation: GOLD Stage 2 (Moderate airflow limitation) reflecting small-airway remodeling and alveolar destruction.

biomarkers.name: Resting Pulse Oximetry (SpO2)
biomarkers.interpretation: Resting arterial desaturation approaching clinical qualification for supplemental home oxygen.

biomarkers.name: 6-Minute Walk Test Distance
biomarkers.interpretation: Significantly diminished functional exercise capacity; independent predictor of hospitalization risk.

stages.title: GOLD 1: Mild Airflow Limitation
stages.criteria: FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 ≥ 80% predicted.
stages.symptoms: Occasional morning cough, mild sputum production, breathlessness on vigorous exertion.
stages.reversibility: Smoking cessation halts accelerated FEV1 loss and restores lung function trajectory towards normal aging.

stages.title: GOLD 2: Moderate Airflow Limitation
stages.criteria: FEV1/FVC < 0.70, 50% ≤ FEV1 < 80% predicted.
stages.symptoms: Exertional dyspnea walking on level ground, frequent winter upper respiratory tract infections.
stages.reversibility: Airway remodeling is irreversible; daily LAMA/LABA maintenance dramatically improves exercise tolerance.

stages.title: GOLD 3: Severe Airflow Limitation
stages.criteria: FEV1/FVC < 0.70, 30% ≤ FEV1 < 50% predicted.
stages.symptoms: Severe breathlessness climbing one flight of stairs, fatigue, recurrent acute exacerbations.
stages.reversibility: High risk of respiratory failure; requires pulmonary rehab, triple therapy (ICS/LABA/LAMA), and rescue plan.

stages.title: GOLD 4: Very Severe Airflow Limitation
stages.criteria: FEV1/FVC < 0.70, FEV1 < 30% predicted OR chronic arterial hypoxemic respiratory failure.
stages.symptoms: Dyspnea at rest, cyanosis, peripheral edema from right heart strain (cor pulmonale), cachexia.
stages.reversibility: End-stage pulmonary disease requiring Long-Term Oxygen Therapy (LTOT), BiPAP, or lung volume reduction surgery.

dos.action: Quit all forms of smoking and vaping immediately and permanently
dos.detail: This is the single intervention proven to slow the rate of FEV1 decline in COPD.

dos.action: Take daily maintenance LAMA/LABA inhalers using correct inhalation technique
dos.detail: Rinse mouth after steroid inhalers; use spacer or check inspiratory flow with dry-powder devices.

dos.action: Practice Pursed-Lip Breathing and diaphragmatic breathing daily
dos.detail: Pursed-lip exhalation creates positive back-pressure, keeping small airways open and releasing trapped air.

dos.action: Keep all vaccinations up to date (Flu, Pneumococcal, COVID, RSV)
dos.detail: Viral and bacterial infections are the root cause of >75% of severe COPD exacerbations.

donts.action: Avoid indoor woodsmoke, incense, chemical aerosols, and heavy air pollution
donts.detail: Particulate matter PM2.5 directly irritates denuded bronchial epithelium, triggering bronchospasm.

donts.action: Never take OTC sedatives, sleeping pills, or opioids without pulmonologist consent
donts.detail: Central nervous system depressants suppress respiratory drive and precipitate acute hypercapnia.

donts.action: Never self-adjust oxygen concentrator settings above prescribed liters/min
donts.detail: Excessive high-flow oxygen blunts hypoxic ventilatory drive in chronic CO2 retainers.

donts.action: Do not ignore increased sputum purulence or worsening shortness of breath
donts.detail: Early initiation of oral corticosteroids and antibiotics within 48 hours prevents ICU admission.

Coronary Artery Disease.description: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) is a pathological fibro-inflammatory condition characterized by the formation of atherosclerotic plaques within the epicardial coronary arteries. Plaque accumulation causes luminal stenosis, restricting oxygenated myocardial perfusion. Plaque rupture or erosion triggers acute platelet aggregation and thrombus formation, culminating in acute coronary syndromes (myocardial infarction) and sudden cardiac death. CAD remains the leading cause of mortality globally.
Coronary Artery Disease.recommended_action: EMERGENCY: If experiencing acute substernal chest pain lasting > 5 minutes, call 911 immediately. For stable symptoms, consult a cardiologist for stress testing, coronary CTA, and aggressive guideline-directed medical therapy.
causes: Apolipoprotein B-containing lipoprotein retention and oxidation in the arterial intima
Endothelial dysfunction driven by hemodynamic shear stress, smoking, and hypertension
Chronic vascular inflammation mediated by macrophage foam cell transformation
Fibrous cap thinning through matrix metalloproteinase degradation by inflammatory cells
Coronary vasospasm and microvascular endothelial dysfunction
symptoms: Radiation of pain to left arm, shoulder, jaw, or epigastrium
Silent ischemia in diabetic and elderly patients
risk_factors: Family history of premature CAD (male <55, female <65)
diagnostic_methods: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram (ECG) to identify ST-segment elevation/depression and T-wave inversion
High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin I/T (hs-cTn) serial assays to rule in/out acute myocardial necrosis
Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography (CCTA) and Coronary Artery Calcium (CAC) scoring
Stress Testing (Exercise ECG, Stress Echocardiography, or Myocardial Perfusion Imaging)
Catheter-based Invasive Coronary Angiography (ICA) with Fractional Flow Reserve (FFR/iFR)
treatment_options: Aggressive Lipid-Lowering: High-intensity Statin (Atorvastatin 80mg) + Ezetimibe + PCSK9 Inhibitor (Evolocumab)
Antiplatelet Therapy: Aspirin 81mg daily + P2Y12 Inhibitor (Ticagrelor or Clopidogrel) post-PCI
Anti-anginal Hemodynamic Regimens: Beta-Blockers (Metoprolol), Calcium Channel Blockers, Nitrates, Ranolazine
Renin-Angiotensin System Blockade: ACEi/ARB for patients with hypertension, diabetes, or LVEF ≤ 40%
Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) with Drug-Eluting Stents (DES)
Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting (CABG) surgery for multi-vessel disease or left main stenosis
prevention_strategies: Achieve stringent LDL-C targets (< 55 mg/dL for secondary prevention, < 70 mg/dL for high risk)
Total smoking cessation (reduces recurrent myocardial infarction risk by 50% within 1 year)
Mediterranean cardioprotective diet rich in extra virgin olive oil, nuts, and omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids
Engage in structured aerobic conditioning (30-60 min/day, 5-7 days/week) within cardiac rehab guidelines
possible_complications: Acute Transmural Myocardial Infarction with cardiogenic shock
Lethal Ventricular Arrhythmias (Ventricular Tachycardia and Ventricular Fibrillation)
Ischemic Cardiomyopathy and chronic congestive heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
Mechanical Complications: Ventricular septal rupture, papillary muscle rupture, cardiac tamponade
Sudden Cardiac Arrest

stages.title: Subclinical Coronary Atherosclerosis
stages.criteria: Positive CAC score (1–99) or non-obstructive plaque on CCTA (<50% stenosis); normal stress test.
stages.symptoms: Completely asymptomatic during daily life and vigorous physical exertion.
stages.reversibility: Plaque progression can be arrested and lipid core volume stabilized with intensive statin therapy.

stages.title: Stable Chronic Coronary Syndrome
stages.criteria: Epicardial stenosis ≥ 50–70% with reversible ischemia on nuclear stress imaging.
stages.symptoms: Predictable chest pressure brought on by vigorous exertion or cold weather, relieved by 5 min rest.
stages.reversibility: Medical therapy + lifestyle halts clinical progression; revascularization indicated if refractory.

stages.title: Unstable High-Risk Coronary Syndrome
stages.criteria: Severe stenosis ≥ 70–90%, thin-cap fibroatheroma (TCFA), fractional flow reserve FFR < 0.80.
stages.symptoms: Angina occurring at rest, accelerating in frequency or duration, or triggered by minimal exertion.
stages.reversibility: Urgent coronary catheterization required to prevent complete thrombotic occlusion and infarction.

stages.title: Acute Myocardial Infarction & Ischemic Heart Failure
stages.criteria: Acute plaque rupture, occlusive intracoronary thrombus, hs-cTn elevation, or LVEF < 40%.
stages.symptoms: Crushing central chest pain > 15 min, diaphoresis, dyspnea, nausea, hypotension.
stages.reversibility: Permanent myocardial necrosis occurs within hours without immediate emergency catheterization (PCI).

early_warning.sign: Exertional retrosternal chest tightness / 'heavy fist'
early_warning.mechanism: Demand-supply myocardial ischemia when heart rate rises past ischemic threshold

early_warning.sign: Atypical radiation of discomfort to left jaw, teeth, or inner arm
early_warning.mechanism: Convergence of cardiac visceral afferent fibers with somatic dermatomes T1-T4 in spinal cord

early_warning.sign: Unexplained dyspnea during mild exertion without chest pain

early_warning.sign: Profound unexplained daytime fatigue and weakness
early_warning.mechanism: Reduced cardiac stroke volume reserve during physiological exertion

acute_emergency.sign: Profuse cold diaphoresis (drenching cold sweat) with nausea
acute_emergency.mechanism: Massive sympathetic adrenergic reflex discharge triggered by cardiogenic shock and myocardial pain

acute_emergency.sign: Acute syncopal collapse or near-fainting
acute_emergency.mechanism: Transient cerebral hypoperfusion from ischemic ventricular arrhythmia (VT/VF) or heart block

acute_emergency.sign: Acute dyspnea with coughing up pink frothy fluid
acute_emergency.mechanism: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema secondary to sudden extensive left ventricular failure

donts.action: Never smoke cigarettes, cigars, or use e-cigarettes

donts.action: Never dismiss recurring chest discomfort as simple 'indigestion' or gas

Healthy / Optimal Baseline.description: Individual exhibits balanced physiological homeostasis across metabolic, cardiovascular, renal, and pulmonary domains. Biomarkers, resting blood pressure, fasting glucose, and lifestyle indices are well within guideline-directed reference intervals, indicating robust cellular resilience, low systemic inflammation, and absence of target organ pathology.
Healthy / Optimal Baseline.recommended_action: Maintain optimal nutritional habits, perform regular aerobic and resistance conditioning (150-300 min/wk), optimize sleep quality (7-8 hrs nightly), and attend routine annual preventive screenings.
causes: Balanced anti-inflammatory nutritional pattern
Consistent daily physical conditioning and zone-2 aerobic endurance
Optimal cellular insulin sensitivity and endothelial nitric oxide production
Restorative circadian rhythm and effective psychological stress management
Absence of toxic exposures (zero tobacco, minimal alcohol)
symptoms: Absence of chronic pain or respiratory complaints
risk_factors: Sedentary episodes during prolonged desk work
